name: Climbing machine
pattern: Vertical climbing: arms and legs drive alternately on a near-vertical track, like climbing a ladder.
setup: VersaClimber: feet in the pedals with straps snug, hands on the handles at about shoulder height.
Jacob's ladder: step onto the lowest rung, hands on the side rails or rungs, belt on if fitted.

steps.text: One hand reaches up as the opposite knee drives up.
Press the other foot down and pull that hand down, standing tall over it.
Swap sides in one smooth rhythm.

cues.cue: Stay upright, hips close to the machine.
cues.why: Leaning back hangs on the arms and loads the lower back.

cues.cue: Push through the whole foot; legs do most of the work.
cues.why: The large leg muscles drive the stroke; climbing uses both arms and legs, which is why it raises oxygen uptake so high.

cues.cue: Long strokes for strength, short fast strokes for sprints.
cues.why: Stroke length and rate set the work; long strokes cover more vertical distance.

cues.cue: Arms pull and push in time with the opposite leg.
cues.why: A cross pattern keeps the trunk stable, as in walking.

breathing: Steady, in rhythm with the strokes; do not hold your breath.

tempo.note: Steady 100-130 steps a minute on a VersaClimber; Jacob's ladder is self-paced.

mistakes.name: Leaning back
mistakes.looks: Hips and shoulders drift away from the machine, arms straight.
mistakes.fix: Pull your hips in and stand tall.
mistakes.why: The arms take your weight and the lower back arches.

mistakes.name: Choppy short strokes all the time
mistakes.looks: Feet only move a few inches.
mistakes.fix: Use the full pedal travel at steady pace.
mistakes.why: Short strokes cut the work done by the hips and legs.

safety: Jacob's ladder: use the belt and step off only when the rungs stop.

variants.change: Pedals and handles on a vertical mast; logs vertical feet and stroke rate.
Rungs on a 40° incline treadmill-style belt; logs vertical feet.
The Compendium has no VersaClimber or Jacob's ladder code. 15538 (treadwall climbing, 10.5 MET) is the closest; for an easy pace use the stair machine, 02065, 9.3 MET.

subtypes.name: VersaClimber
subtypes.change: Body near vertical, short to long pedal strokes.

subtypes.name: Jacob's ladder
subtypes.change: Body leans forward about 40° with the ladder; hands climb the rungs.

motion.basis: No kinematic study found for either machine. All angles are estimates from the machine geometry; cross (opposite arm and leg) pattern is coaching convention.

sources.cite: Brahler CJ, Blank SE. VersaClimbing elicits higher VO2max than does treadmill running or rowing ergometry. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 1995;27(2):249-254.
Haff GG, Triplett NT (eds). Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning, 4th ed. NSCA / Human Kinetics, 2016.
